title: Full-stack work in one capsule: FastAPI, PostgreSQL 17 and React

overview.summary: A developer opens a todo application in VSCodium inside a DevCapsule, finishes its backend endpoint and its React handler, starts the stack from the editor's terminal, uses the application in Chromium on the same desktop, and checks with `psql` that the rows are in PostgreSQL.
overview.intent: This end-to-end test shows that one isolated capsule is enough for full-stack work. The editor, Python, Node, the PostgreSQL client and the browser all come from what the project declares; the developer installs none of them.
illustrates: The project declares its needs (`python`, `node`, `postgresql-client`, `browser-automation` and a frontend IDE) and the capsule provides them.
The editor, its terminal and the browser share one contained desktop, shown in your browser. The capsule uses no display of the host.
Backend, frontend and database tools work together inside the capsule: FastAPI on `:18080`, Vite on `:15173`, `psql` against PostgreSQL 17.
The result is checked from outside: after the recording, the test reads the same four rows from the API and from PostgreSQL.

stack.name: Database
stack.detail: PostgreSQL 17 in a container the test starts beside the capsule, database `tododb` on `127.0.0.1:15432`

stack.name: Browser
stack.detail: Chromium, from `browser-automation`, on the capsule's desktop

steps.title: Open the workspace in VSCodium inside the capsule
steps.action: Launch the project's capsule, trust the workspace when VSCodium asks, and look at the project: `.devcapsule/`, `backend/` and `frontend/`.
steps.expected: VSCodium fills the capsule's `1600×1000` desktop with the workspace loaded and trusted.

captions.text: VSCodium is open on the capsule's desktop, with the project in the explorer.
Trust the workspace, so the editor's features are all enabled.

steps.title: Implement `POST /api/todos` in the FastAPI backend
steps.action: Quick-open `backend/main.py` (`Ctrl+P`), go to line 75 (`Ctrl+G`) inside `create_todo`, type the parameterized `INSERT INTO todos … RETURNING` query and the JSON response, and save (`Ctrl+S`).
steps.expected: `backend/main.py` holds the finished insert handler, saved, with no unsaved mark on its tab.

captions.text: Go to Line (`Ctrl+G`) jumps to line 75, inside `create_todo`.
Type the handler: a parameterized `INSERT … RETURNING`, then the row as JSON.
Save (`Ctrl+S`). The endpoint that creates a task is complete.

steps.title: Implement `handleCreate` in the React frontend
steps.action: Quick-open `frontend/src/App.jsx` (`Ctrl+P`), go to line 30 (`Ctrl+G`) inside `handleCreate`, type the `fetch('/api/todos', { method: 'POST', … })` request and the `setTodos` update, and save (`Ctrl+S`).
steps.expected: `frontend/src/App.jsx` holds the finished `fetch` call and state update, saved.

captions.text: Go to Line (`Ctrl+G`) jumps to line 30, inside `handleCreate`.
Type the handler: `POST` the new task to `/api/todos`, then add the returned row to the list.
Save (`Ctrl+S`). The form now talks to the backend.

steps.title: Check PostgreSQL 17 and start the stack from the editor's terminal
steps.action: Open VSCodium's integrated terminal (`` Ctrl+` ``) and run `./run-stack.sh`: it checks PostgreSQL 17 with `psql`, starts Uvicorn on `:18080` and starts Vite on `:15173`.
steps.expected: The terminal prints the PostgreSQL 17 version, the two seeded rows as `psql` reads them, and `STACK_READY`.

captions.text: `./run-stack.sh` checks PostgreSQL 17 with `psql`, starts FastAPI and Vite, and ends on `STACK_READY`.

steps.title: Open the application in Chromium on the capsule's desktop
steps.action: Launch Chromium on the capsule's own display, beside VSCodium, at `http://127.0.0.1:15173`.
steps.expected: **CapsuleTask** shows `PostgreSQL 17.11 · Connected`, its counters, and the two seeded tasks, `pg#1` and `pg#2`.

captions.text: Chromium opens CapsuleTask inside the capsule: PostgreSQL is connected and two seeded tasks are listed.

steps.title: Create two tasks and complete one in the browser
steps.action: Type *Record FastAPI + React customer pitch demo* and click **Add Task**; type *Verify PostgreSQL 17 persistence across reloads*, choose the *Database* category and click **Add Task**; then tick the checkbox of `pg#1`.
steps.expected: Both tasks appear at once with the identifiers PostgreSQL gave them, `pg#3` and `pg#4`, and the counters read 4 tasks, 2 completed.

captions.text: Add a first task. It appears at once as `pg#3`, the identifier PostgreSQL returned.
Add a second task in the *Database* category: `pg#4`.
Tick `pg#1`. The Completed counter goes to 2.

steps.title: Reload from PostgreSQL and ask the database directly
steps.action: Click **Refresh from DB**, switch to VSCodium's terminal and run `./query-db.sh`, then return to **CapsuleTask**.
steps.expected: `psql` and the browser agree: four rows, `1` to `4`, with completion flags `t, t, f, f`.

captions.text: **Refresh from DB** reloads the list from PostgreSQL: 4 rows.
In VSCodium's terminal, `./query-db.sh` asks PostgreSQL directly: the same four rows, two of them completed.
Back in CapsuleTask: what the browser shows is what the database holds.
